notes: 20-item bank. CAPS mix: 8 L2 / 8 L3 / 4 L4. Topics: % change (increase/decrease), reverse VAT, reverse markup, find original. SA contexts: petrol price, salary raise, sale prices, VAT-inclusive totals.

stimulus.inline: % change = (new − old) ÷ old × 100.

items.question: A litre of petrol rose from R20 to R23. Calculate the % increase.

stimulus.inline: % decrease uses the original (old) value as the divisor.

items.question: A laptop priced at R8 000 was reduced to R6 800. Calculate the % decrease.

stimulus.inline: Always divide change by the OLD value, not the new one.

items.question: Mrs Pillay's monthly salary rose from R12 000 to R13 200. Calculate the % increase.

stimulus.inline: A negative change means a decrease.

items.question: A bakkie was bought for R250 000 and sold 3 years later for R200 000. Calculate the % decrease in value.

stimulus.inline: A scholarship pays R12 500 per year, up from R10 000 last year.

items.question: Calculate the % increase from last year.

stimulus.inline: Calculate % change using (new − old) ÷ old × 100.

items.question: A water-tank reading rose from 8 200 L to 9 020 L in a week. Calculate the % increase.

stimulus.inline: Round % change to one decimal place when not exact.

items.question: School enrolment fell from 950 to 893 learners. Calculate the % decrease to 1 decimal place.

stimulus.inline: A spaza shop's monthly profit fell from R6 800 to R5 100.

items.question: Calculate the % decrease.

stimulus.inline: A VAT-inclusive amount = original × 1,15. So original = VAT-incl ÷ 1,15.

items.question: A till slip's VAT-inclusive total is R287,50. Calculate the original (VAT-exclusive) amount.

stimulus.inline: Reverse % increase: original = new ÷ (1 + r/100).

items.question: After a 20% sale discount, a jersey costs R320. Calculate the original (pre-discount) price.

stimulus.inline: After a salary raise, you know the new amount and the % raise.

items.question: After an 8% raise, Mr Khoza now earns R16 200 per month. Calculate his previous salary.

stimulus.inline: % change in 2 steps.

items.question: Petrol rose from R23,50 to R25,40. Calculate the % increase to 1 decimal place.

stimulus.inline: Reverse a markup: selling price = cost × (1 + markup%/100).

items.question: A retailer sells a kettle for R368 after a 15% markup. Calculate the cost price.

stimulus.inline: Difference in % growth between two values can be compared.

items.question: Suburb A's population grew from 10 000 to 11 500. Suburb B's grew from 8 000 to 9 200. Which had the higher % growth?

stimulus.inline: Find the original value given the final value and a % decrease.

items.question: A car's value depreciated by 30% to reach R140 000. Calculate the original value.

stimulus.inline: Cell-phone contract: now R649 after a 10% loyalty discount.

items.question: Calculate the original (full-price) monthly contract fee.

stimulus.inline: A learner is told: 'A salary rose 10%, then fell 10%. Therefore it's back to the original.'

items.question: Starting from R20 000, what is the final salary, and is the learner correct?
workingSteps: Final = R19 800. The learner is wrong — successive % changes don't cancel because the base changes.

stimulus.inline: A small business reports revenue of R55 200 in March, up from R48 000 in February. Critique the claim: 'This is the same as a 15% increase.'

items.question: Calculate the actual % increase to 1 decimal place and judge the claim.
options: Claim is approximately right — actual is 15,0%.
items.expectedAnswer: Claim is approximately right — actual is 15,0%.
workingSteps: Claim is correct to one decimal place.

stimulus.inline: A car insurance premium rose 5% in 2024 and a further 7% in 2025. Original premium R450/month.

items.question: Calculate the 2025 premium, then the OVERALL % increase from the original.

stimulus.inline: A grocer marks bread up by 20% over cost. The selling price is R23,40.

items.question: Calculate (a) the cost price and (b) the rand profit per loaf.

_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_PERCENT_CHANGE_DIVISOR: Divides change by the NEW value instead of the OLD value.
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_PERCENT_REVERSE_NAIVE: Subtracts/adds a % of the new amount instead of dividing by (1 ± r/100) to recover the original.
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_PERCENT_SUCCESSIVE_ADD: Adds two successive percentage changes (treats them as additive when they compound on a changing base).
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_ROUND_NEAREST_RULE: Misapplies the rounding rule on the final answer.
